incentives.name: Qualified data center sales and use tax exemption and reduced electricity rate
incentives.what: Qualified data centers (at least $100M invested over up to three years and 15 net new full-time jobs, lowered in 2016 from $250M and 25 jobs) buy computer equipment, repair services, backup power infrastructure and cooling equipment free of sales tax and pay a reduced 1.5% state sales tax rate on electricity. One application per location.
incentives.value_known: No dollar cost published. Department of Revenue told Rep. Behn the state has 25 exemptions but will not name recipients, citing taxpayer confidentiality.

incentives.name: FastTrack grants and job tax credits (general programs)
incentives.what: Data centers are eligible for ECD FastTrack grants and tax credits; ECD says no data center has received FastTrack funds and tax credits are confidential.

dockets.regulator: Tennessee Valley Authority Board of Directors (federal; not the Tennessee Public Utility Commission, which does not regulate TVA or its local power companies)
dockets.utility: TVA / Memphis Light, Gas and Water
dockets.what: TVA board approved a deal letting xAI's Memphis-area data center operations buy up to 300 MW of power (reported as doubling xAI's supply).

dockets.regulator: Tennessee Valley Authority Board of Directors (federal)
dockets.utility: TVA and its local power companies
dockets.what: TVA board approved a separate data center rate class at its Memphis meeting: data centers leave the manufacturing class and fall into four categories by contract demand; applies to new and existing facilities from Oct. 1, 2026, phased in over three fiscal years; average bill impact about 10% (CFO Tom Rice). New or expanding data centers above 5 MW pay a capacity commitment charge of about $1.5M per MW over three to five years. Residential rates unchanged. Proposed in May 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: SB2128 (Taylor) / HB1847 (Butler), 2026: data center power cost bill
laws_and_bills.what: Owners of data centers needing at least 50 MW must pay for infrastructure upgrades needed to serve them; utilities cannot pass those costs to other ratepayers unless upgrades also benefit them or follow normal large-customer rules. Also lets data centers self-generate (e.g., gas turbines) or buy from independent power producers without state or local oversight.

laws_and_bills.name: SB2653 (Taylor) / HB2392 (Reneau), 2026: Tennessee Data Center Impact Review Act
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required water and wastewater operator board permits and reporting of water sources and daily, peak and annual use. Sent to general subcommittee, no vote.

laws_and_bills.name: SB2112 (Campbell) / HB2456 (Pearson), 2026
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required data centers to register with the Department of Revenue and report fuel, electricity and water use. Failed in House Business and Utilities Subcommittee March 18, 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: SB1682 (Lamar) / HB2061 (Towns), 2026
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required registration with the Public Utility Commission and reporting of electricity and water use and rates. Failed for lack of a second in Senate Commerce and Labor, March 3, 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: SB1999 (Lamar) / HB2054 (Camper), 2026: Data Center, Artificial Intelligence and Clean Transition Tariff Accountability Act
laws_and_bills.what: Would have set tariffs for large energy-intensive users and required them to fund incremental generation and grid upgrades. Never advanced to a vote.

laws_and_bills.name: SB1832 (Yarbro) / HB1461 (Clemmons), 2026
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required high performance computing facilities to devote 50% of output to public benefit and report carbon footprint annually. Failed 2-6 in House Agriculture and Natural Resources Subcommittee, March 3, 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: SB2584 (Jackson) / HB2047 (McCalmon), 2026
laws_and_bills.what: Data centers receiving certain tax credits would have had to certify no WARN, FLSA or federal immigration violations in the prior year. Fizzled in Senate committees.

laws_and_bills.name: Rep. Aftyn Behn proposal for 2027 session: three-year pause on data center sales tax exemption certificates
laws_and_bills.what: Announced plan to file a bill halting new exemption certificates for three years and requiring the Department of Revenue to report annual cost, holders, compliance and revocations. Not yet filed as of the source date.

local_rules.what: 18-month moratorium on data center permitting, passed unanimously by the Board of Mayor and Aldermen.
Data center moratorium passed unanimously (at least one year per Tennessee Lookout).
County moratorium on the June 2026 commission agenda; vote expected June 22, 2026.
BL2026-1448 (Councilmember Courtney Johnston): moratorium on new data center permits through Dec 1, 2026.
BL2026-1391 and BL2026-1392 (lead sponsor Rollin Horton): zoning rules for data centers, including distance requirements from sensitive uses, by size and megawatts.

12-month pause on data center rezoning applications, site plan approvals and building permits (sponsor J.B. Smiley Jr.); would not apply to existing xAI data centers. Advanced from committee Aug 18, 2026; council voted Oct 6 to delay the final vote to Oct 20, 2026. At the contentious Oct 6, 2026 meeting the council deferred the vote; the council chair then barred Rep. Justin J. Pearson and others from the Oct 10 and Nov 10 meetings, and Pearson sued the city on Oct 15 (Tennessee Lookout, https://tennesseelookout.com/2026/10/15/rep-pearson-sues-memphis-alleging-first-amendment-violation/).
City council approved a 60-day pause on new data center applications on July 28, 2026; the planning commission recommended a 12-month moratorium on Aug 25, 2026.
local_rules.status: 60-day pause enacted 2026-07-28; 12-month moratorium recommended, final council vote not confirmed
